Let me recommend a few short books that I love:

Penpal by Dathan Auerbach (great horror, told in a series of connected short stories which give you a stopping point to take breaks if you need them, and overall the book isn't very long)

Angel Dust Apocalypse by Jeremy Robert Johnson (this is an anthology of bizarro fiction that's utterly fantastic and memorable--it features a lot of intense imagery, so if you're not into that then you might not like it)

Darkly Dreaming Dexter by Jeff Lindsay (this is what the Showtime series Dexter is based off of, but the books are 1000x better and their plots/characterizations are vastly different, especially from the second book onwards; it's kind of like a crime thriller with a strangely likable serial killer protagonist)

On Writing by Stephen King (this book is less than 300 pages long and it had a huge effect on me--it's non-fiction and it serves as a combination of Stephen King's memoirs and his writing tips; there are 100+ books listed in the back that he recommends for anyone who loves to write/read, so you get a reading list from one of the world's most successful authors, and he has decent taste in my opinion)

The Mirrored Heavens by David Williams (fast-paced, semi-realistic sci-fi action thriller--it has two sequels and I read the entire trilogy in about a week's time, as I found all three together at a Goodwill)

The Dogs of Babel by Carolyn Parkhurst (part mystery, part examination of grief, and part tragedy/drama--this is the only book to ever make me cry, and I just so happened to be reading it in public at the time, so be prepared to sob like a child)

1984 by George Orwell (this is an absolute dystopian classic and if you haven't read it then you should do so immediately--you can probably find the text online somewhere with little to no trouble, as it's public domain in some non-US countries, like Canada)

Brave New World by Aldous Huxley (another dystopian classic; Huxley was actually Orwell's French teacher, believe it or not, and the two of them were friends who would sometimes debate about whose vision of dystopia was more accurate)

The King in Yellow by Robert W. Chambers (this is a weird fiction anthology - "weird fiction" being the genre, not a descriptor, but I suppose it works for both - and it served as a large inspiration for Lovecraft; DEFINITELY public domain and available for free online, as well as free on Amazon Kindle)

Herbert West: Reanimator by Howard Phillips Lovecraft (this is a novella, so it's very short--you can read it for free at the link I've provided, or you can buy Lovecraft's complete works here if you want something physical)

John Dies at the End by David Wong (wonderful comedy/horror hybrid about a drug called Soy Sauce; beware this author's recent works, as he's been getting increasingly political--this is a hefty book at around 600 pages, but the rest I gave you were really short, and I figured you'd need something longer eventually)

Sorry if that's too many. I just wanted to give you a lot of options/genres/styles to look at. I hope I've helped!
